items.title: Beeble Releases SwitchHDR, an AI Model for HDR Reconstruction From SDR Video
items.excerpt: Beeble has released SwitchHDR, a new frontier AI model that reconstructs HDR imagery from conventional SDR video — promising a way to bring dynamic range into footage that never had it, for post, delivery and restoration workflows.
items.why: A concrete new AI craft tool for colorists and finishing artists; HDR-from-SDR reconstruction changes remastering and deliverable pipelines.
items.notes: Beeble's earlier Canvas compositor (May 20) is stale; SwitchHDR is the new release. Pairs naturally with the Corridor Crew social item, which uses Beeble's platform.

items.title: Midjourney Seeks to Reveal Studios' Use of AI in High-Stakes Copyright Battle
items.excerpt: Midjourney is appealing a magistrate judge's order limiting discovery into how Disney, Universal and Warner Bros. themselves use AI in their shows and movies, seeking to put studios' internal AI use on the record as part of its fair-use defense.
items.why: Turns the studios-vs-AI lawsuit inside out: Hollywood's own quiet AI adoption becomes evidence, shaping how openly studios can use generative tools.
items.notes: Carryover from the 07-07 pool — verified fresh again and still not published as a card.

items.title: What You Need to Know About A24's Partnership with Google DeepMind
items.excerpt: No Film School unpacks A24's $75M research partnership with Google DeepMind — what the studio actually gets (AI storyboard tools, DeepMind researchers working alongside filmmakers) and whether the 'AI is infecting Hollywood' panic fits the facts.
items.why: The most consequential studio-AI deal of the moment, explained from a filmmaker-workflow angle rather than a business one.
items.notes: Same story family as a24-defends-google (Deadline) and a24-still-cool (THR) — curator should pick ONE A24 angle. Original Variety announcement (06-22) fell just outside the 336h window.

items.title: A24 Defends Google AI Partnership: "We'd Rather Have a Seat at the Table"
items.excerpt: After a wave of backlash and boycott calls, A24 defended its Google DeepMind deal as a research partnership — working side-by-side with DeepMind researchers to shape new tools and workflows while filmmakers keep full creative control.
items.why: The studio's own framing of how AI research embeds into a creative org — a template other studios will copy or avoid.
items.notes: Same story family as a24-google-deepmind-explainer (NFS) and a24-still-cool (THR).

items.title: Is A24 Still Cool? Boycott Calls Follow the Google DeepMind AI Deal
items.excerpt: THR examines how the indie darling's Google DeepMind AI partnership triggered boycott calls from its own fanbase — and what it says about an era when any Big Tech association can smoke-bomb even the most beloved creative brands.
items.why: Brand-trust fallout of AI adoption: how a design-forward studio's audience reacts when AI enters the pipeline.
items.notes: Same story family as the two A24 items above — pick one of the three.

items.title: This AI-Powered Music Assistant Can Watch You Edit and Suggest Tracks as You Work
items.excerpt: Soundstripe LIVE is billed as the first AI music assistant that watches editors work inside Premiere, Final Cut Pro or DaVinci Resolve and suggests licensed tracks that fit the scene as the cut takes shape — music supervision folded into the edit itself.
items.why: Ambient, in-context AI assistance inside the NLE — a new interaction pattern for editorial workflows beyond prompt boxes.
items.notes: NFS at per-source cap (3) with this item; NFS Peppa Pig piece dropped for the cap (THR covers that story below).

items.title: Hasbro's TV Contracts Allegedly Ask Child Voice Actors to Sign Rights Away for AI Use
items.excerpt: Hasbro's contracts for shows including Peppa Pig allegedly ask child voice actors to sign away rights for AI use of their voices; a UK agents' association warns a parent's approval 'should never be a blanket licence to capture, clone, train, or reuse a child's voice indefinitely.'
items.why: Voice cloning consent hits its sharpest edge case — minors — setting precedents for likeness/voice rights across screen production.
items.notes: NFS's 'Peppa Pig AI tipping point' (06-25) is the same story; THR original kept for the wider funnel.

items.title: So we invented a way to cheat... (Corridor Crew's AI VFX workflow with Beeble)
items.excerpt: Corridor Crew reveals the AI VFX workflow behind their new season: Beeble's SwitchLight AI relighting plus their own CorridorKey keying let them composite actors into scenes without a traditional green-screen pipeline.
items.why: A high-craft creator team showing, shot by shot, how AI relighting/keying replaces a legacy VFX pipeline — practical AX for filmmakers.
items.notes: Published time from channel RSS and watch-page datePublished (2026-07-05T09:00:26-07:00). Pairs with the beeble-switchhdr news item — fine to run both (tool news vs workflow demo) or pick one.

items.title: How to "Vibe Direct" Short Films
items.excerpt: Hands-on with 'vibe directing': Matt Wolfe builds a horror movie trailer in OpenArt Director by describing story, characters, pacing and voice performances in a chat, then refining everything conversationally — up to 5-minute films from dialogue alone.
items.why: Shows the conversational-direction interaction model in practice, from the creator side rather than the vendor announcement.
items.notes: CAUTION: OpenArt's vibe-directing tool itself was the 07-06 THR card — this is a practical-demo angle on the same tool. Use only if the curator wants the hands-on follow-up; otherwise skip as near-dupe.
